questions.question: When filling a two-event Venn diagram, the region to fill FIRST is:
options: The overlap — because each event's total already includes it
Any region; order does not matter

questions.question: In the survey (40 learners; 22 soccer, 15 chess, 9 both), the soccer-ONLY region holds:
The 'neither' region of that diagram holds:
The final check on any completed Venn diagram is that:
options: The two circles are the same size
The overlap is the smallest number
Each circle totals the sample space
All four regions together total the sample space — here 13 + 9 + 6 + 12 = 40

questions.question: The addition rule states:
options: $P(A \text{ or } B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B)$

questions.question: For the survey, $P(\text{soccer or chess})$ equals:
The subtracted term in the addition rule removes:
options: The learners who play neither game
The overlap, which the addition of the two whole events counted twice

questions.question: Given $P(A) = 0{,}45$, $P(B) = 0{,}3$ and $P(A \text{ or } B) = 0{,}6$, then $P(A \text{ and } B)$ is:
Two events are mutually exclusive when:
options: They cover the whole sample space
They share no outcomes — they cannot both happen on the same trial

questions.question: On a Venn diagram, mutually exclusive events appear as:
options: Two circles with no overlapping region

questions.question: On one die roll, A = 'less than 3' and B = 'at least 5'. $P(A \text{ or } B)$ is:
options: $\dfrac{2}{6} + \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, since the events share no outcome

questions.question: Dropping the subtraction for events that DO overlap is dangerous because the answer:
options: Is inflated by the double-counted overlap — and can even exceed 1

subtopics.title: Complementary Events and Full Machinery Problems

questions.question: Complementary events are events that are:
options: Mutually exclusive AND exhaustive — no overlap, and together they cover the whole sample space

questions.question: 'Less than 3' and 'at least 5' on a die are mutually exclusive but NOT complementary because:
options: The outcomes 3 and 4 belong to neither event, so the pair fails to cover the sample space

questions.question: For the survey, $P(\text{neither})$ computed via the complement of 'soccer or chess' is:
options: $1 - \dfrac{7}{10} = \dfrac{3}{10}$, matching the 12 out of 40 in the outside region

questions.question: The probability that a surveyed learner plays EXACTLY ONE of the two games is:
In the playground picture, a learner who plays both games stands:
options: With one foot in each separate hoop
In the lens where the two hoops overlap — inside both at once
In whichever hoop they joined first

questions.question: The both-players walk to the overlap FIRST because:
options: The overlap is the biggest region
The outside grass must be filled last
Each club's total already includes them, so the 'only' regions can only be found by subtracting them out

questions.question: A learner standing inside the rectangle but outside both hoops represents:
options: A class member who plays neither game — still part of the sample space

questions.question: Adding the clipboards (22 + 15 = 37) disagrees with the 28 learners standing in hoops because:
options: The nine both-players are written on both clipboards, so their bodies were counted twice
Chess players refuse to stand in hoops

questions.question: The one-sentence version of the addition rule is:
options: Add the clubs, then double the shared members
Subtract the clubs from the class
Add the two clubs, then subtract the shared members once, because the addition greeted them twice
Multiply the clubs and divide by the class

questions.question: A computed 'P(A or B)' greater than 1 is a warning that:
options: The sample space is too small
An overlap was double-counted — the subtraction was skipped on overlapping events

questions.question: Hoops pulled completely apart, with some learners still on the outside grass, model events that are:
The 'outside-grass test' says events are COMPLEMENTARY only when:
options: The grass region is the largest
Both hoops are the same size
Nobody stands outside and nobody stands in an overlap — a perfect two-way split of everyone
At least one learner stands outside

questions.question: With $P(A) = 0{,}4$ and $P(B) = 0{,}35$ mutually exclusive, $P(\text{neither } A \text{ nor } B)$ is:
